reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first final pass. Reopened the adopted Scandinavia programme’s aims, credit table and home-alternative footnote, then the actual Danish language, literature, exchange, translation, regional-research and thesis entries before comparing that source-led account with the exact finished decision/canonical. Reconsidered the actual workbook contents and 48-course trial ledger against the region-centred target. This is a separate pass by the same AI, not an independent person or live app inspection.
findings: The adopted OER B1 confirms the Dutch full-time BA, RIO 56807, formal Scandinavia Studies track. Danish is the first complete main-language choice in the current guide; no Norwegian or Swedish branch is added. The programme has 60+60+60 unique EC: 36 common plus 24 Danish in year one, 24 home units plus 30 exchange plus 6 sociolinguistic research in year two, and 18 thematic/translation plus 30 open plus 12 graduation project in year three. The recurrent tutoring and diagnostic carry zero credits.

The dated Danish sequence satisfies attendance/completion requirements in its actual order. Literature requires the completed Danish first year and reads nineteenth- to twenty-first-century texts in Danish. Danish 5 requires Danish 4 passed and includes 3 EC Danish plus 1.5 each receptive Norwegian and Swedish within its six EC. Languages of the North requires attendance in language 1–3; Vikings follows language 1–4 and Modern Scandinavia. The sociolinguistic project follows all language preparation and Languages of the North. OER B4.4 requires positive BSA; faculty A6.4/A6.6 gives the ordinary full-time 48-EC threshold.

The adopted Appendix 1 and course 57868 require 30 EC in the second-year exchange window; they control the public page’s generic optional-third-year paragraph. Copenhagen is first in the detailed course’s Danish-compatible host order. The route completes 60 first-year EC and the first semester of year two before departure, exceeding the stated 54-EC preparation. Courses must follow the regional cultural-history, language/translation or literature lines; main Scandinavian language proficiency cannot count. A home alternative requires Board approval and is not stacked. No host course names are invented.

Translation requires Danish 1–5 completed. Rewriting the North and National Identities extend Nordic memory, representation, politics and cultural interpretation; their Scandinavian group uses the languages prepared earlier. The thesis requires the first year plus at least 54 second-year EC; full year-two completion meets it. Its 8,000–10,000 words concern a Scandinavian regional, linguistic, literary or cultural question within supervisory expertise. The January proposal workshop is not extra credits. The writing-language rule is conditional on assessed B2/C1 proficiency, with Dutch otherwise. Thirty open EC remain separate under OER B5, including level, external approval, overlap and optional-placement limits.

The defining subject is sustained regional inquiry, not language acquisition alone: modern Scandinavian political/social/cultural history, regional literature and translation, language variation and intelligibility, nineteenth-century-to-present identities, and contemporary North/Arctic and Sami/Inuit questions. General comparative humanities methods are a real part of the target and were fully considered; they do not erase its regional object.

The first trial combines psycholinguistics, stylistics, rhetoric, literary and media analysis, qualitative methods and social theory. The second combines full literary work with comparative history, gender/Indigenous identities, media and visual heritage; the third tests Nordic social-system interests through welfare economics, public health, democratic and EU institutions, policy, modern history and social research. Norse myth is explicitly supported in the current official World Myth description. The actual methods and subject contributions in all 48 trial courses are acknowledged. Their combined teaching nevertheless becomes general language/cultural inquiry or European social science rather than sustained Nordic study. No Nordic-course quota, disciplinary-equivalence rule, licence test or requirement that each non-PPD course teach the region is imposed.

All three 24-course trials pass current workbook feasibility, including the only planned Psycholinguistics term after Brain and Behaviour, first-year PPD and at least six advanced courses. Planning coverage is present. Initial fall-capacity conflicts were repaired without restoring offerings; schedule failure is not the no-match reason. The old brief-Sweden claim is not corroborated by current comparative-politics evidence and is not inherited. Description-only courses were read and assessed within what their descriptions support.

All sixty interest rows were reconciled: fifteen generators have explicit coherent trial ownership, twenty-nine topics support, and sixteen examples/outcomes remain search-only. No career claim generates a programme. Read the English record/index title, two selected paragraphs, year and Danish/Copenhagen label, all twenty component titles and credits and eleven selected notes in renderer context. The exception displays complete external-only content and the supported no-match reason. No UCR course-description modal, programme, concept, alignment or optional research is active. Academic, mechanical and content findings satisfy record-content-review-2026-10-31; no runtime or release approval is claimed.
